source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 274 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 274.

PD 274.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 274 was established by Ordinance No. 19625, passed by the Dallas City Council on August 12, 1987. Ordinance No. 19625 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 274 is established on property generally located along the south line of Arapaho Road, east of the east line of Prestonwood Boulevard. The size of PD 274 is approximately 11.387 acres. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A. (Ord. 25711)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.104. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 274A). (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission prior to the issuance of a building permit for any use on the Property and must comply with the conceptual plan and the provisions of this article. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Landscape Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.106. LANDSCAPE PLAN.

A landscape plan must be approved by the city plan commission prior to the issuance of a building permit for any use on the Property. Landscaping must be installed in accordance with the approved landscape plan within six months of the date of issuance of any certificate of occupancy for any use on the Property. All landscaping must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition at all times. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Permitted Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.107. PERMITTED USES.

Use of the Property is limited to the following:

(1) A retirement home use. For the purposes of this article, a retirement home use means a multiple-family use for retirement families. For the purposes of this article, retirement family means two persons or fewer, one of whom is age 60 or older, living together as a single household unit.

(2) A personal care home use. For the purposes of this article, a personal care home use means a facility that furnishes room, board, laundry, and other services of a personal care nature such as assistance with personal hygiene and grooming. A personal care home does not provide medical, nursing, or custodial care.

(3) An adult activities center use of 3,500 square feet of floor area or less. For the purposes of this article, and adult activities center use means a facility that offers recreational activities for persons who reside on the premise.

(4) A nursing home use.

(5) Retail and personal services uses of 7,000 square feet of floor area.

(6) Multiple-family uses.

(7) A private recreational club or area use. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Maximum Number Of Units
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.108. MAXIMUM NUMBER OF UNITS.

A retirement home use is limited to a maximum of 354 units. A personal care home use is limited to a maximum of 200 units. A nursing home use is limited to a maximum of 100 beds. A retirement home use, personal care home use, and nursing home use are limited to a maximum of 390 units/beds combined. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Minimum Lot Area
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.109. MINIMUM LOT AREA.

Multiple-family uses must meet the minimum lot area requirements for an MF-1(A) district. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Minimum Setbacks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.110. MINIMUM SETBACKS.

All structures must meet the setback requirements of an MF-1(A) district. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Maximum Coverage
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.111. MAXIMUM COVERAGE.

Coverage of the Property may not exceed 290,000 square feet of floor area for all structures combined. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Maximum Permitted Height
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.112. MAXIMUM PERMITTED HEIGHT.

Maximum permitted height for any structure on the Property is 40 feet. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.113. OFF-STREET PARKING.

(a) Parking for the retirement home use and personal care home use is required at the ratio of 0.7 spaces per dwelling unit plus one space per employee position. All other uses must provide parking as required in Chapter 51A.

(b) A parking structure serving a retirement home use, personal care home use, or nursing home use is prohibited on the Property. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Off-Site Improvements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.114. OFF-SITE IMPROVEMENTS.

(a) Prior to the issuance of a building permit for any use on the Property, the owner shall submit a cash payment or a letter of credit, approved by the city attorney’s office and submitted to the director of public works and transportation for the following improvements. If any of the improvements are undertaken with public funds, the owner shall reimburse the city for its specified share of the improvement prior to the issuance of a building permit. If, after a period of ten years from the time of payment of a fee, any portion of the money has not been spent for the specified improvement, the remaining portion of the fee paid must be refunded to the payor of his assignee.

(b) The owner shall fund the consolidation and realignment of the driveway on Belt Line Road as illustrated in Exhibit 274B and installation of a traffic signal based on the proportionate amount of traffic that the development will contribute to the southbound approach as determined by the director of public works and transportation through a Transportation Engineering Study to be provided by the applicant prior to the issuance of any building permit on the Property.

(c) The combined cost of the two improvements shall not exceed a maximum of $30,000.00. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.115. SIGNS.

Signs will meet the requirements for non-business zoning districts contained in Section 51A- 7.400, except that one detached sign is permitted on each street frontage that meets the requirements for non-business zoning districts. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: General Requirements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.116. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

Development of the Property within this PD must comply with the requirements of all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Paving
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.117. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.118. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or certificate of occupancy for a use in this PD until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other applicable ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-274.119. ZONING MAP.

PD 274 is located on Zoning Map No. B-7. (Ord. Nos. 19625; 25711)
